attempts.plan:
1. Read the borough table (33 rows) and neighbor-list file into pandas DataFrames.  

2. Handle missing values:  
   • The one borough with either first-half or second-half value missing will be DROPPED from every subsequent calculation (ensures every observation used has a valid change value).  
   • The same borough will also be removed from the neighbor graph; edges that referenced it are deleted.  
   → Final working sample size N = 32.

3. Calculate CHANGE = second_half_2014_value − first_half_2014_value for each remaining borough.

4. Build a symmetric binary spatial-weight matrix W (N×N):  
   • w_ij = 1 if boroughs i and j are listed as neighbors, else 0; w_ii = 0.  
   • Store S0 = Σ_i Σ_j w_ij (needed for Moran’s I).  
   • Do not row-standardize (classical Moran’s I definition).

5. Compute Global Moran’s I for the CHANGE variable:  
   I = (N / S0) · [Σ_i Σ_j w_ij (x_i − x̄)(x_j − x̄)] / [Σ_i (x_i − x̄)²]  
   where x_i is CHANGE and x̄ its mean.

6. Assess significance via a Monte-Carlo permutation test:  
   • Repeat 999 random permutations of the CHANGE values among borough labels (≥500 as required).  
   • Recalculate Moran’s I for each permutation to form the reference distribution.  
   • Two-tailed p-value = (count of |I_perm| ≥ |I_obs| + 1) / (999 + 1).

7. Interpret:  
   • If p < 0.05 and I_obs > 0 ⇒ similar-direction changes cluster spatially (CLUSTERED).  
   • If p < 0.05 and I_obs < 0 ⇒ neighboring boroughs tend to change in opposite directions (DISPERSED, but we will still label NOT CLUSTERED per instructions).  
   • If p ≥ 0.05 ⇒ no spatial association (NOT CLUSTERED).

8. Report:  
   • Quote the observed Moran’s I (rounded to 3-4 decimals) and permutation p-value (rounded to 3 decimals).  
   • Conclude with the required single-line format:
     FINAL ANSWER: CLUSTERED/NOT CLUSTERED (test statistic = <value>, p = <value>)

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, random, os, math

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA_PATH = "chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_no2crime_crime_first_half_2014_to_second_half_2014.csv"
ADJ_PATH  = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

df   = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)
adj  = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Drop borough(s) with a missing value in either period
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=["first_half_2014_value", "second_half_2014_value"]).copy()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. CHANGE variable
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
df_clean["change"] = df_clean["second_half_2014_value"] - df_clean["first_half_2014_value"]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Build a symmetric binary weight matrix ------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
valid_boroughs = set(df_clean["borough"])
adj_filt = adj[adj["borough"].isin(valid_boroughs) & adj["neighbor"].isin(valid_boroughs)]

# index lookup
borough_to_idx = {b:i for i,b in enumerate(df_clean["borough"])}
N = len(borough_to_idx)

W = np.zeros((N,N), dtype=np.float64)
for _, row in adj_filt.iterrows():
    i, j = borough_to_idx[row["borough"]], borough_to_idx[row["neighbor"]]
    W[i,j] = 1
    W[j,i] = 1   # ensure symmetry

np.fill_diagonal(W, 0)

S0 = W.sum()          # Σ_i Σ_j  w_ij

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Global Moran's I  ---------------------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
x     = df_clean["change"].to_numpy()
x_bar = x.mean()
x_dev = x - x_bar

numerator   = x_dev @ W @ x_dev          # Σ_i Σ_j w_ij (x_i- x̄)(x_j- x̄)
denominator = (x_dev ** 2).sum()         # Σ_i (x_i - x̄)^2
I_obs = (N / S0) * numerator / denominator

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Permutation test (999 random shuffles) ------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
n_perm = 999
I_perm = np.empty(n_perm)

rng = np.random.default_rng()            # NumPy 1.17+ generator
for k in range(n_perm):
    x_perm = rng.permutation(x_dev)      # permute deviations
    I_perm[k] = (N / S0) * (x_perm @ W @ x_perm) / denominator

p_two_tailed = (np.sum(np.abs(I_perm) >= abs(I_obs)) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Decide verdict -------------------------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
if p_two_tailed < 0.05 and I_obs > 0:
    verdict = "CLUSTERED"
else:
    verdict = "NOT CLUSTERED"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Print exactly what is required --------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"data_points_used = {N}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (Moran's I = {I_obs:.5f}, p = {p_two_tailed:.5f})")
